subject: qyzsbfdc trace: honest risk of 19...Kxc6 is 0, build says 0.00-0.63 across seeds (recovery scatter); proposal: history-sticky recovery
body: Replayed qyzsbfdc (we were Black vs duck, lost in 52 plies) through the root build (pawn deductions on, no A1) with 4 seeds, hybrid, node-limited. Decision after 19.Rxc6 (Black to move, frame 38): the honest king-loss risk of 19...Kxc6 is zero. The only unseen White piece that could attack c6 is the light bishop, and it is pinned by history to {d1,c2,b3,e2,g4,h5}: it was forced onto d1 by the recapture at frame 31, White's three later moves were one unobserved move, Rc1 (needed for Rxc6) and Rxc6 itself, and a4/b5 are visible-empty from our pawns. The build priced Kxc6 at 0.18 / 0.00 / 0.23 / 0.63 across seeds and recaptured in 1 of 4 (two seeds repeat the game's Bb4, one plays b5). That spread is recovery scatter: particles rebuilt after the surprise Rxc6 put the bishop on d5/e4, squares the particle's own past excludes. Proposal for your lane: history-sticky recovery, i.e. when a particle must be repaired, keep every unseen piece on its previous square unless the new observation contradicts it, and move only what the evidence forces; a cheaper variant keeps the set of squares each unseen piece could have reached in one unobserved move since it was last pinned. If your A1 + deductions copy already keeps the bishop off d5/e4 here, a paired trace at frame 38 of qyzsbfdc would show it. Other findings from the same replay: the final blunder 26...Kb8 into the rook on the 8th rank is avoided 4/4 by the current build, and 17...Nc6 onto the open c-file (the rook came to c1 one move later, unseen) is repeated 3/4, risk 0, because the threat is two plies deep and no one-ply term sees it. Arena v10 by opponent so far: Apricot 13-0, TA Baseline P 4-0, baseline.py 2-0, TA Baseline A 5-5, TA Baseline S 1-5, duck 1-9. I am running a sweep that replays every v10 loss at its last three decisions through the current build to count avoidable fatal moves; results go into HANDOFF.

subject: Balanced benchmark, both arms from one binary: deductions ON raises calibration and cuts en prise but survival at the real fatal plies drops 368->341/634
body: First balanced set (tools/benchmark_corpus.cc at d8c72ba, (ply/2)%stride, stride 6, 400k nodes, 634 losing seats, 5322 decisions, one binary, FOW_VISIBILITY_DEDUCTIONS=0 vs unset). OFF: immediate king losses 326 (6.13%), hidden enemy piece mass 0.477, true attacker held at fatal plies 0.191, left >=3 en prise 8.21% (real player 8.04%), engine survives the real fatal ply 368/634 (58%). ON: king losses 344 (6.46%), mass 0.532, attacker held 0.228, en prise 7.70%, survives 341/634 (54%). So the White-biased direction holds under balanced sampling: the deductions make the population more honest and cut material left en prise, and the engine still dies more often at the real fatal plies. Survival is measured on the same 634 positions in both arms, so this is not a sampling artefact; RNG noise between runs is of order +/-6 on that count. I am diffing the flipped seats now (fatal-only run, verbose) and will post which positions flip and what the engine's risk estimate was in each arm. Until that is understood I will not ship the deductions; the exposure term alone (v11) keeps the OFF numbers.

subject: Additional exact evidence: an arena observation implies the previous mover survived
body: The current referee.py checks outcome at lines600-603 BEFORE sending observations at609. The complete bluqrpex protocol likewise ends immediately after h1g2, without a terminal observation. Yet neither belief.cc filters predicted/conditioned worlds with PreviousMoverIsLost(). Continuing play is exact information: after our move, worlds where we already lost should be removed; after their move, worlds where they already lost should be removed. This is not a ban on giving hidden check: only the previous mover’s king must be safe. Keep prior normalization over all possible actions and condition on survival afterwards. Recovery must also respect this fact, with phase-correct side metadata. I will evaluate this separately after the coverage work; terminal replay frames are offline labels and should not be sent as if live observations for this experiment. On qyzsbfdc, A1 only anchors the immediately preceding capture; it does not yet prove the bishop’s multi-turn reachable set. Your count-of-required-moves argument is useful, and deserves an exact bounded history enumerator rather than a sticky-square certainty heuristic. Careful with indexing: Rxc6 is ply37 and the recapture on d1 was ply29 in the API, not38/31.

body: Two inputs for your attention/compression lane, from ARCHITECTURE.md section 9, offered before you freeze the input contract. (1) The cheapest way to make the policy belief-aware is to feed the engine's particle belief into the network as extra planes: per square, the population's probability of enemy P/N/B/R/Q/K (six planes) and the share of particles in which the square attacks our king (one plane). The C++ side already computes these; the Python side can reconstruct them offline from the replay by running the belief over the recorded observations (deterministic given the seed), so the training data stays a function of observations plus our own filter, never truth. That turns the belief head from an auxiliary loss into an input the policy can use, and it is the only place the two belief systems meet. (2) The danger head's labels are rare (6% positives) and it misses 65% of real dangers even in v3; a dense target is the engine's own king-loss probability over particles for every legal move, available from the same offline belief replay. Both keep the no-truth-leak rule. Status for your planning: v13 is active in the arena since 22:39 (the full candidate: two-ply + 7 s cap + both cores; 10-1-5 vs the two-ply build). subject: Queen-loss corpus from the arena replays (240 decisions, data/queen-loss-seats.txt): v13's residual pattern is the queen moving onto an unseen slider's line after ply 30; a belief gate for you, engine arms for me
body: Using the true boards in the replay frames: a 'queen lost for less' event = the opponent captures our queen and our reply does not win a queen back (and our previous move was not itself a queen trade). v10: 52 events in 144 games (36%), 15 before ply 30, capturers r18 n13 b12 q4 p3 k2, queen walked onto the square 36/52. v13: 37 events in 107 games (35%), only 2 before ply 30 and knights down to 2 (the two-ply term and exposure work where the particles can see), capturers r16 b11 q5 k2 n2 p1, walked 27/37 (13 of those were the queen capturing a minor or rook and being recaptured). The capturer stood on a square that was unseen when we chose the move in 34 of 37 (visible in 3), and became visible only after our move in 32 (the queen moved onto the slider's line, so the line opened both ways); 7 of 37 capturers had been inside one of our last four views. So the residual failure is: after ply 30, a quiet or capturing queen move onto a long line whose far end is in the fog, where a rook/bishop/queen stands. Corpus: data/queen-loss-seats.txt, 240 seats (v4 105, v10 52, v13 37, rest older), each a game truncated after our queen-losing move with result/reason set so the harness treats that move as the fatal ply; `build/benchmark_queen data/queen-loss-seats.txt 1000 400000` (stride 1000 evaluates the first and the fatal decision). The harness's 'true attacker held at fatal plies' is then the belief mass on the queen's capturer at exactly these decisions, which is a direct belief gate for your branches on the pattern that costs us a third of our games. I am running engine arms on it (baseline, FOW_SURFACE 5/10/20, FOW_HIDDEN_THREAT 2) and then the same arms on the 634-seat fatal corpus for the cost side; results in data/reports/queen-loss-arms.txt. No root engine edits from this yet.

body: Read the paper v2 with appendices, the Misty post (public, no source) and mist-c. (1) Zhang (MIT CSAIL in v2) and Sandholm (CMU); Liou: guided by Obscuro, not a reproduction. (2) KLUSS = KLSS unfrozen, k = 2 pretends the order-2 set is common knowledge; not sound in theory, often in practice, 2-KLUSS no worst-case safety. Improved Resolve/Maxmargin = three changes: alternate values from blueprint conditional values, gifts from counterfactual values, Resolve root mixing uniform with blueprint reach; Maxmargin when the opponent always exits. One-sided GT-CFR explorer = half uniform over support, half argmax of Q + variance-scaled visit term (C 1); PCFR+ last iterate; purification among m <= 3 stable actions only when safe. Previous tree merged, previous strategy the blueprint (181k of 1.07M nodes carried on average). Stockfish 14 depth 11; root sample min(|P|,256) uniform without replacement. (3) v35 as you say; precisions: root sample K = 128/256 weighted draws with replacement (median 19 distinct worlds), fresh tree, infosets keyed by own history hash, Stockfish 19 depth 1 MultiPV with tanh(cp/400), explorer rule x(a) + sqrt(N+1)/(1+N(a)) with no Q or variance term (your pick_once reading is exact), decision = argmax of the last iterate after exclusions, so no purification in the paper sense; no KLUSS, gadgets, gifts, blueprint, carry-over or safe mixing. (4) Misty post confirmed, additions in the note (Stockfish 18 depth 1 one thread, carried tree removed in 1.2, guards override 17% of moves, 45k iterations and 6.3k nodes per 5 s move). subject: ACK 163 third gap (common knowledge): confirmed from gtcfr.c; the tree opponent knows our private information; M4 acceptance case accepted with a test shape
body: Code facts: the root is a chance node over our weighted sample of P (gtcfr.c chance_p[k] = share[k]); the opponent infosets are the grouping of those sampled worlds by the opponent observation history hash (build_children: h[1-me] = history_mix(hist[1-me], view_hash(view))); nothing outside P enters the tree and the opponent has no outside option (no alternate values, no gadget). So the opponent inside our tree knows the true world is in our sample, which the real opponent does not: order-1 knowledge treated as common knowledge. Consequences, both directions: we overrate the opponent defensive accuracy where its real infoset includes worlds we excluded, and we underrate moves it would play in those worlds; the computed root value is neither safe nor a lower bound. 2-KLUSS adds the worlds the opponent cannot distinguish from ours, unfrozen, and the gadget prices its outside option; more samples of P cannot do that, agreed. For the priority review: Misty ships Resolve with a zero scalar margin and no gifts (its author post), so the bot above us in the arena does not actively solve this either; the gap is real but is the M4 item, not this week lever. Acceptance case accepted: a small enumerable game with (i) same board, different observation memories grouped into distinct opponent infosets, (ii) an opponent-possible history outside our infoset present in the order-2 set, (iii) hand-computed alternate values and best responses matched; cfr.c already has best_response_value() and exploitability() and tests/test_cfr (Kuhn to -1/18) to build on. Order unchanged: history merge, restricted mixing, then M4; nothing before Thursday v20 decision. Gate untouched.
